one_line: A cosmopolitan South Indian guild merchant of many lands, moving between nagaram market towns and Bay of Bengal ports in the 10th–13th centuries.

appearance.age_look: Mid-30s, lean but sturdy build, used to travel and negotiation.
appearance.face: Oval face with medium-brown Dravidian complexion, sharp nose, neatly groomed short beard and moustache, thoughtful almond-shaped eyes with a calm, assessing gaze, faint forehead lines from squinting in sun, default expression a composed half-smile of measured confidence.
appearance.hair: Thick black hair parted in the middle and pulled back into a low knot at the nape, wrapped in a narrow pale-cream cloth band (simple headband) over the knot; hair at the front smooth and tidy, sideburns short.
appearance.costume: Era-accurate South Indian merchant attire: an unbleached off-white cotton angavastra-style upper cloth draped over both shoulders and around the torso, worn over a long ankle-length veshti/dhoti in muted indigo-dyed cotton with a simple narrow maroon border, pleated in front and wrapped securely at the waist; beneath, a barely visible pale cotton inner tunic; around his waist a sturdy brown leather belt (for pouches) sitting over the dhoti; on his shoulders, a secondary light shawl in soft turmeric-yellow with a subtle thin green stripe near the edge, hinting at guild prestige; simple leather sandals suited to long walking; jewellery limited to a thin gold chain with a small round pendant, a single practical copper bangle on the right wrist, and small plain gold stud earrings; a cloth money-pouch and palm-leaf document case hang at his right hip from the belt.
appearance.signature: A rolled bundle of palm-leaf documents tied with a reddish-brown cord and sealed with a small clay seal, held in his left hand as his constant prop symbolizing contracts, guild letters, and temple endowments.

ref_desc: A mid-30s medium-brown South Indian merchant with a low-knotted black hairstyle and cream headband, wearing an off-white upper cloth, indigo dhoti with maroon border, yellow-striped shawl, simple jewellery and belt, holding rolled palm-leaf documents tied with cord.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of a mid-30s South Indian Nanadesi merchant from the 10th–13th century: medium-brown complexion, oval face, sharp nose, short beard and moustache, calm almond eyes and a composed, thoughtful half-smile; thick black hair parted in the middle, pulled into a low knot at the nape wrapped with a narrow pale-cream cloth headband. He wears an unbleached off-white cotton upper cloth draped over both shoulders and around his torso, a long ankle-length indigo cotton dhoti with a simple narrow maroon border neatly pleated in front, and a light turmeric-yellow shawl with thin green stripes near the edge over one shoulder, all in modest, historically plausible South Indian textiles. A sturdy brown leather belt sits over the dhoti holding a cloth money-pouch and a palm-leaf document case at his right hip, and he stands in simple brown leather sandals; jewellery is minimal: a thin gold chain with a small round pendant, a single copper bangle on his right wrist, and small plain gold stud earrings. His signature prop is a rolled bundle of palm-leaf documents tied with a reddish-brown cord and showing a small clay seal, held confidently in his left hand; use a palette of off-white, indigo blue, maroon, turmeric yellow, and brown, and present him front-facing with clear view of face, hair, clothing layers, belt, pouches, and documents for consistent redrawing.
